summary: Russian forces conducted multiple drone and missile attacks across Ukraine, targeting civilian infrastructure in Zaporozhye, Kramatorsk, and other regions, resulting in casualties and structural damage. Ukraine reported reduced Russian missile production due to strikes on defense facilities. Political developments include Keir Starmer's resignation as UK Prime Minister and Endy Berman's appointment, with continued Western support pledged. (Source: @UkraineNow/82791)
key_points: Russian forces attacked Zaporozhye and Kramatorsk with drones and missiles, killing at least two and injuring several civilians, damaging multi-story buildings. (Source: @UkraineNow/82791)
Maryna Bezuhla was appointed as a senior commander, replacing an unnamed predecessor. (Source: @eRadarrua/101821)
Russian Iskander-M missile production decreased to 50-55 per month due to Ukrainian strikes on defense industries. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69272)
Anti-drone nets were deployed in Zaporozhye to counter Russian UAV threats. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31763)
Russian forces claimed to have captured Ukrainian soldiers from the 'Skelya' regiment during operations in Kostyantynivka. (Source: @UkraineNow/82792)
Keir Starmer resigned as UK Prime Minister, succeeded by Endy Berman, who reaffirmed support for Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/82795)
Russian forces targeted Nova Poshta warehouses in Kharkiv region, according to unverified reports. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31753)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces continue to escalate drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, with increased activity in Zaporozhye, Kharkiv, and Belgorod regions. Reduced Iskander-M production suggests Ukrainian strikes on Russian defense facilities are having operational impact. Russian forces are leveraging captured Ukrainian soldiers for propaganda to demoralize Ukrainian society. Continued Western support, including UK leadership changes and Canadian military aid, may offset some logistical challenges. (Source: @UkraineNow/82791)
sections.regional_response: Western allies, including Canada and the UK, continue military support for Ukraine despite political transitions. EU countries like Greece, Germany, and France oppose additional sanctions, signaling potential shifts in economic commitment. Political changes in Europe, including upcoming elections, may affect long-term support for Ukraine. Russian forces are targeting civilian infrastructure to strain Ukrainian resources and morale. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31761)
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian forces are using captured Ukrainian soldiers for information warfare, as seen in Kostyantynivka operations. Anti-drone measures in Zaporozhye indicate adaptive Ukrainian defensive strategies. Political instability in Europe, including UK leadership changes, may influence future support for Ukraine. Russian forces are targeting logistics and civilian infrastructure to disrupt Ukrainian operations. (Source: @UkraineNow/82792)
